label: Theorized Nigerian women’s anti-colonial mobilization into Stiwanism
description: Inheriting Ransome-Kuti’s Abeokuta grassroots women’s struggle, Ogundipe articulated Stiwanism to anchor African feminism in collective social transformation.
dialecticalTension: Translates Nigerian anti-colonial women’s praxis into systematic African feminist theory.

citations.author: Molara Ogundipe
citations.work: Re-Creating Ourselves: African Women & Critical Transformations

label: Critiqued Western individualistic feminism for ignoring colonial class and kinship realities
description: While engaging global feminist theory, Ogundipe rejected Euro-American models that isolate gender from neocolonialism, race, and communal African sociality.
dialecticalTension: Replaces Western individualist emancipation with Social Transformation Including Women in Africa.

label: Formulated Stiwanism as endogenous African feminist framework
description: Ogundipe coined STIWA (Social Transformation Including Women in Africa) to center African women’s structural empowerment alongside men against neocolonial inequities.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes gender equity with anti-imperial communal transformation.
